item.title: [Injury] Chris Youngblood (POR): Chris Youngblood (foot) has been ruled out against the Kings on Friday.
item.description:
Chris Youngblood (foot) has been ruled out against the Kings on Friday.

Youngblood will miss a second straight game, which should allow Sidy Cissoko and Scoot Henderson to take on a few extra minutes. However, neither should see a dramatic boost in production from Youngblood’s absence. Cissoko is already starting and had 19 points on Wednesday.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Injury] Cam Christie (LAC): Cam Christie (ankle) is not on the injury report for Friday’s game against the Thunder.
item.description:
Cam Christie (ankle) is not on the injury report for Friday’s game against the Thunder.

Christie will be back following a one-game absence. However, his role has been minimal this season, so his return won’t impact the Clippers’ rotation.

item.title: [Injury] Jaylin Williams (OKC): Jaylin Williams (back) has been ruled out against the Clippers on Friday.
item.description:
Jaylin Williams (back) has been ruled out against the Clippers on Friday.

Williams will remain sidelined for a sixth straight game. Aday Mara has been starting recently and has taken on extra minutes with Williams unavailable, which is a trend that should continue against LA.

item.title: [Injury] Ajay Mitchell (OKC): Ajay Mitchell (ankle) is questionable to play against the Clippers on Friday.
item.description:
Ajay Mitchell (ankle) is questionable to play against the Clippers on Friday.

Mitchell missed Wednesday’s game against Portland, which allowed Alex Caruso to slide into the starting unit. Caruso contributed 14 points, three steals and four triples in the loss and would be worth streaming if Mitchell ends up missing another game.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Injury] Mouhamed Gueye (ATL): Mouhamed Gueye has progressed to on-court activities and will be re-evaluated in four weeks.
item.description:
Mouhamed Gueye has progressed to on-court activities and will be re-evaluated in four weeks.

The latest update has Gueye progressing in the right direction, with his next evaluation scheduled for some time around Dec. 10. Gueye will be a solid depth forward for Atlanta, but he’ll only make a fantasy impact if there is an injury to someone in front of him.

Noah Rubin

Fonte: Hawks PR

item.title: Dean Wade (PHI): Tyrese Maxey, VJ Edgecombe, Jaylen Brown, Dean Wade and Joel Embiid will start against the Raptors on Thursday.
item.description:
Tyrese Maxey, VJ Edgecombe, Jaylen Brown, Dean Wade and Joel Embiid will start against the Raptors on Thursday.

Wade will get the starting nod with LeBron James sidelined. This will likely be a singular start for Wade, though the 76ers do have a back-to-back coming up on Sunday and Monday, so Wade could be in line for another start.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Injury] Joel Embiid (PHI): Joel Embiid (foot) is available to play against the Raptors on Thursday.
item.description:
Joel Embiid (foot) is available to play against the Raptors on Thursday.

Embiid will be good to go despite the initial questionable tag after seemingly tweaking his foot in Tuesday’s loss. He’ll occupy his usual spot in the starting unit.

item.description:
Morez Johnson Jr. (shin) is available to play against the Timberwolves on Thursday.

Johnson will be back following a one-game absence. That allowed Santi Aldama to take on a larger role off the bench. With Johnson back, both players will need minutes, which will likely limit the fantasy impact of both players.

item.description:
Bryce McGowens (elbow) is doubtful to play against the Grizzlies on Friday.

McGowens has taken on extra minutes over the last two games, but he hasn’t been part of the Pelicans’ rotation for most of the year. His absence won’t open the door for anyone to step into legit minutes.

item.title: [Injury] Maxime Raynaud (SAC): Kings insider James Ham reports that Maxime Raynaud (knee) is progressing but has no official timeline to return.
item.description:
Kings insider James Ham reports that Maxime Raynaud (knee) is progressing but has no official timeline to return.

The backup big man has yet to make his season debut, but until he returns, Dylan Cardwell and Precious Achiuwa should continue to pickup the slack in the frontcourt.

item.title: [Injury] Bennedict Mathurin (NOP): Bennedict Mathurin (thumb) is doubtful to play against the Grizzlies on Friday.
item.description:
Bennedict Mathurin (thumb) is doubtful to play against the Grizzlies on Friday.

Mathurin is expected to miss a second straight game with this thumb injury. Jordan Poole played 21 minutes in Mathurin’s absence on Wednesday and should provide most of the offense off the bench once again in this one. He scored 14 points in their last game and has upside, but Poole isn’t a reliable option.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Injury] Trey Murphy (NOP): Trey Murphy (knee) and Yves Missi (knee) are doubtful for Friday’s matchup with the Grizzlies.
item.description:
Trey Murphy (knee) and Yves Missi (knee) are doubtful for Friday’s matchup with the Grizzlies.

Murphy will miss a third straight game, and Missi will be sidelined for an 11th straight. With the pair expected to sit out against Memphis, Saddiq Bey and Karlo Matkovic should continue to handle additional playing time.

item.description:
LeBron James (sciatica) is out for Thursday’s matchup with the Raptors.

item.title: [Injury] Klay Thompson (MIA): Miami Heat insider Ira Winderman reports that Klay Thompson (ankle) and Pelle Larsson (illness) missed Thursday’s practice.
item.description:
Miami Heat insider Ira Winderman reports that Klay Thompson (ankle) and Pelle Larsson (illness) missed Thursday’s practice.

According to Winderman, Thompson injured his ankle on a chase-down block in Tuesday’s matchup with the Jazz. If both Thompson and Larsson end up sitting out Friday’s matchup with the Cavaliers, more minutes could be available for Tim Hardaway Jr. and Andrew Wiggins.

item.description:
Moussa Diabaté (quad) is available for Thursday’s matchup with the Suns.

Grant Williams (hamstring) will make his season debut Thursday against the Suns.

item.description:
Scottie Barnes (adductor) is out for Thursday’s matchup with the 76ers.

Barnes will miss a fourth straight game while dealing with a left groin strain. That should mean another start for Collin Murray-Boyles, who has averaged 13.8 points, 5.8 rebounds, 1.8 assists and 2.0 “stocks” across his last four starts.

item.title: [Injury] Stephen Curry (GSW): ESPN’s Shams Charania reports that Steph Curry sustained an oblique abdominal tear and will be re-evaluated in two weeks.
item.description:
ESPN’s Shams Charania reports that Steph Curry sustained an oblique abdominal tear and will be re-evaluated in two weeks.

Curry sustained the injury in Wednesday’s loss to Houston, and it will keep him out until late November at minimum. In Curry’s absence, De’Anthony Melton should handle an expanded role after logging 25 minutes Wednesday after Curry’s early exit. Will Richard could also see some additional playing time until Curry returns.

Zak Hanshew

Fonte: Shams Charania

item.title: [Recap] Aday Mara (OKC): Aday Mara notched 11 points (4-of-8 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), six rebounds, two assists and one block in Wednesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.
item.description:
Aday Mara notched 11 points (4-of-8 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), six rebounds, two assists and one block in Wednesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.

For the first time in his young NBA career, Mara played over 30 minutes in a game. He logged 32 minutes against the Trail Blazers, but the final stat line wasn’t strong enough to make the rookie a must-start in all leagues. Mara replaced Kenrich Williams (11/2/2 with one block and two three-pointers) in the starting lineup, and who starts moving forward may be dictated by the opposition’s rotation.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Alex Caruso (OKC): Alex Caruso accounted for 14 points (4-of-6 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, three steals and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.
item.description:
Alex Caruso accounted for 14 points (4-of-6 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, three steals and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.

The Thunder didn’t have Ajay Mitchell for Wednesday’s game, opening a spot in the starting lineup for Caruso. He took advantage of the opportunity, shooting 4-of-5 from beyond the arc. Caruso’s 14 points were a new season high for him, as he totaled 17 points in the first four games he played upon returning from an ankle injury. If Mitchell remains out for Friday’s game against the Clippers, Caruso would be worth rostering in 14-team leagues and some 12-team leagues.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Isaiah Hartenstein (OKC): Isaiah Hartenstein accumulated 20 points (10-of-14 FGs), 11 rebounds, six assists and two steals in Wednesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.
item.description:
Isaiah Hartenstein accumulated 20 points (10-of-14 FGs), 11 rebounds, six assists and two steals in Wednesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.

After totaling 19 points in Oklahoma City’s first five games of November, Hartenstein recorded his first 20-point game of the season on Wednesday. The negative for iHart was the turnovers, of which he was responsible for six. A few of the turnovers were due to offensive fouls, so there isn’t much to worry about there. Rostered in 83 percent of Yahoo leagues, Hartenstein is providing top-100 fantasy value, slightly better than his ADP.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Shai Gilgeous-Alexander (OKC): Shai Gilgeous-Alexander produced 31 points (9-of-20 FGs, 13-of-14 FTs), four rebounds, two assists and one steal in Wednesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.
item.description:
Shai Gilgeous-Alexander produced 31 points (9-of-20 FGs, 13-of-14 FTs), four rebounds, two assists and one steal in Wednesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.

Gilgeous-Alexander has scored at least 30 points in six games this season. Unfortunately for him and the Thunder, the team’s lack of established scorers proved costly in both losses to the Trail Blazers. Five other Thunder players scored in double figures, with Isaiah Hartenstein’s 20 leading the way. The lack of creators who can take some of the pressure off of Gilgeous-Alexander was evident in both losses to the Trail Blazers. He’ll remain an elite fantasy option, but SGA’s ceiling may have taken a slight hit because a few of his teammates are injured.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Jrue Holiday (POR): Jrue Holiday accumulated 19 points (5-of-12 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), three rebounds, five assists, two steals and five three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Thunder.
item.description:
Jrue Holiday accumulated 19 points (5-of-12 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), three rebounds, five assists, two steals and five three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Thunder.

A double-digit scorer in seven straight games, Holiday provided solid fantasy value on Wednesday. In addition to the 19 points, he shot 5-of-8 from beyond the arc and recorded good numbers in assists and steals. Through 11 games, Holiday has been close to a top-100 fantasy player, something most managers did not expect before the season began.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Sidy Cissoko (POR): Sidy Cissoko produced 19 points (6-of-9 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), two rebounds and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Thunder.
item.description:
Sidy Cissoko produced 19 points (6-of-9 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), two rebounds and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Thunder.

Replacing Scoot Henderson (5/2/2 with one three-pointer) in the starting lineup ahead of Tuesday’s win over the Thunder, Cissoko played well in both victories. The Trail Blazers wing totaled 36 points, five rebounds, three assists, one steal and seven three-pointers in Portland’s two-game sweep of Oklahoma City. While Cissoko isn’t a must-add player right now, he’s worth watching in deep leagues to see if the last two games were a fluke.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Damian Lillard (POR): Damian Lillard recorded 18 points (5-of-14 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), three rebounds, three assists, one steal and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Thunder.
item.description:
Damian Lillard recorded 18 points (5-of-14 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), three rebounds, three assists, one steal and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Thunder.

While Lillard didn’t lead the way offensively for the Trail Blazers as he did in Wednesday’s win over Oklahoma City, the production remained solid. He’s scored at least 20 points in seven of Portland’s first 11 games, and Dame has started every game. As long as he stays healthy, Lillard should be able to deliver a top-100 season, if not more.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Deni Avdija (POR): Deni Avdija tallied 28 points (9-of-20 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), three rebounds, six assists, four steals, two blocks and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Thunder.
item.description:
Deni Avdija tallied 28 points (9-of-20 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), three rebounds, six assists, four steals, two blocks and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Thunder.

One night removed from scoring 24 points in a win over the Thunder, Avdija was just as productive in the rematch. The 28 points were the most he’s scored in a game since November 2, when the Trail Blazers forward hit that number in a win over the Nuggets. While there were questions before the season began about Portland’s offensive pecking order, there haven’t been any issues so far, even when the currently injured Ja Morant was healthy. That’s great for those who used a top-50 draft pick on Avdija.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] De'Anthony Melton (GSW): De’Anthony Melton finished Wednesday’s loss to the Rockets with 11 points (3-of-7 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, four assists, one block and three three-pointers.
item.description:
De’Anthony Melton finished Wednesday’s loss to the Rockets with 11 points (3-of-7 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, four assists, one block and three three-pointers.

Melton’s final stat line wasn’t much to write home about, but his role may expand for Friday’s game against the Spurs. Stephen Curry left Wednesday’s game with an abdominal injury and is expected to undergo an MRI on Thursday. If Curry misses time, Melton will have a larger role, whether he moves into the starting lineup or continues to come off the bench.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Brandin Podziemski (GSW): Brandin Podziemski accounted for 22 points (7-of-15 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), six rebounds, four assists, two steals and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Rockets.
item.description:
Brandin Podziemski accounted for 22 points (7-of-15 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), six rebounds, four assists, two steals and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Rockets.

For the first time this season, Podziemski has scored at least 20 points in consecutive games. He finished with a solid stat line, missing only a blocked shot. And the Warriors may need even more from Podziemski in the short term, as Stephen Curry left Wednesday’s game with an abdominal injury.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Darryn Peterson (UTA): Darryn Peterson got himself 22 points (7-of-19 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), four rebounds, five assists, a steal, a block, and two 3-pointers in 123-108 loss to the Magic.
item.description:
Darryn Peterson got himself 22 points (7-of-19 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), four rebounds, five assists, a steal, a block, and two 3-pointers in 123-108 loss to the Magic.

Over the past week, Darryn Peterson has gotten more confident, aggressive, and the Jazz have been letting him lose. The peripheral stats from college have started to come back, and it’s been exciting to watch. You want more in terms of efficiency, but with Lauri Markkanen out for a month, Darryn is a must roster if he hasn’t been picked up in your league already.

Brian Taylor

item.title: [Recap] Ace Bailey (UTA): Ace Bailey put up 18 points (6-of-17 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, two steals, four blocks, and three 3-pointers in loss on Wednesday.
item.description:
Ace Bailey put up 18 points (6-of-17 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, two steals, four blocks, and three 3-pointers in loss on Wednesday.

Ace Bailey has been great this season and has been one of the best shot blockers in the NBA. His ability to havoc defender at this point is a great sign for his long-term development. He’s coachable and is a great teammate. The efficiency wasn’t great in this one, but it’s hard to complain with the peripheral stats that he gave you in this one.

Brian Taylor

item.title: [Recap] Brice Sensabaugh (UTA): Brice Senabaugh scored 19 points (6-of-10 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), three rebounds, an assist, a steal, a block, and three 3-pointers in loss to the Magic.
item.description:
Brice Senabaugh scored 19 points (6-of-10 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), three rebounds, an assist, a steal, a block, and three 3-pointers in loss to the Magic.

Brice Sensabaugh has had a rough month of November, but it was good to see a bounce back game from the scoring department. Sensabaugh kept the Jazz afloat in the fourth quarter on the offensive end when the Magic shut off the water on everyone else. He remains a stream guy for points and 3’s in redraft leagues, but not a high priority one.

Brian Taylor

item.title: [Recap] Anthony Black (ORL): Anthony Black put up 22 points (6-of-14 FGs, 7-of-9 FTs), seven rebounds, eight assists, a steal, and three 3-pointers in win against the Jazz on Wednesday.
item.description:
Anthony Black put up 22 points (6-of-14 FGs, 7-of-9 FTs), seven rebounds, eight assists, a steal, and three 3-pointers in win against the Jazz on Wednesday.

Back-to-Back great games against the Kings and the Jazz. He was aggressive in looking for his shot and it helped lead them to the win. This season, he’s been awesome from a statistical perspective and hitting his 3’s. The Magic are going to need to make a decision to trade one of their core places if they want to keep him around.

Brian Taylor

item.title: [Recap] Desmond Bane (ORL): Desmond Bane scored 25 points (9-of-16 FGs), three rebounds, two assists, a steal, and seven 3-pointers in win on Wednesday.
item.description:
Desmond Bane scored 25 points (9-of-16 FGs), three rebounds, two assists, a steal, and seven 3-pointers in win on Wednesday.

Desmond Bane’s 3PT shooting was a massive weapon to the Magic in this one and was a big reason why the Magic were able to pull away in the fourth quarter. You would want more in the peripheral stats, but this is about what you would expect from Desmond Bane on a night-to-night basis.

item.title: [Recap] Franz Wagner (ORL): Franz Wagner with a monster 38 points (13-of-23 FGs, 9-of-10 FTs), eight rebounds, an assist, a steal, and three 3-pointers in a 123-108 win over the Jazz on Wednesday.
item.description:
Franz Wagner with a monster 38 points (13-of-23 FGs, 9-of-10 FTs), eight rebounds, an assist, a steal, and three 3-pointers in a 123-108 win over the Jazz on Wednesday.

Franz Wagner led the way for the Magic in this one and he really helped spearhead this offense. These are the types of performances that you want as a Franz owner without Paolo. It’s easier when you’re going against the Jazz, but it’s good see him hit some 3’s in this one. He started talking smack to the Jazz and really got going in the fourth quarter.

Brian Taylor

item.title: [Recap] Marcus Smart (HOU): Marcus Smart was ejected from Wednesday’s game against the Warriors with 21 seconds left in the third quarter.
item.description:
Marcus Smart was ejected from Wednesday’s game against the Warriors with 21 seconds left in the third quarter.

Smart’s night ended prematurely after getting tangled up with Warriors center Charles Bassey late in the third quarter. The Rockets guard threw a punch that grazed Bassey’s nose. Smart finished with six points (2-of-2 FGs), two rebounds, one assist and two three-pointers. If he’s suspended, Reed Sheppard should get more minutes.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Ty Jerome (MEM): Ty Jerome had 22 points (9-of-18 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), two rebounds, five assists, and a three in loss on Wednesday.
item.description:
Ty Jerome had 22 points (9-of-18 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), two rebounds, five assists, and a three in loss on Wednesday.

Jerome has had 5 straight games of at least 20 points which is awesome for fantasy owners. He led the team with a +9 in a five point loss. If you got Jerome at ADP, you got an absolute monster of a steal on draft day. Unless he gets traded, there’s no sign of this slowing down. He fits very well with this team and he’s really contributing to winning.

Brian Taylor

item.title: [Recap] Jaylen Wells (MEM): Jaylen Wells scored 22 points (6-of-13 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), two rebounds, an assist, and five 3-pointers in loss to the Nuggets on Wednesday.
item.description:
Jaylen Wells scored 22 points (6-of-13 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), two rebounds, an assist, and five 3-pointers in loss to the Nuggets on Wednesday.

Jaylen’s shot making is what kept Memphis in this game with his 3PT shooting. His game is pretty empty apart from the 3’s and the points, but he’s still a very valuable player as a threat as a shooter. His value as an NBA player is very stable with how the NBA wants these wings shooters that can play good defense.

Brian Taylor

item.title: [Recap] Jaime Jaquez (MIL): Jaime Jaquez Jr. tallied 25 points (7-of-16 FGs, 9-of-9 FTs), five rebounds, three assists, two steals and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Lakers.
item.description:
Jaime Jaquez Jr. tallied 25 points (7-of-16 FGs, 9-of-9 FTs), five rebounds, three assists, two steals and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Lakers.

After starting each of Milwaukee’s first 11 games, Jaquez was moved to the bench on Wednesday. Given his productivity, that may be a role the Bucks ask Jaquez to take on moving forward. Recording his first 20-point game since October 24 against the 76ers, Jaquez finished with a season-high 25 as part of a solid overall stat line. He was runner-up for NBA Sixth Man of the Year last season, so this isn’t a foreign role for Jaquez. And it may raise his fantasy ceiling if the Bucks continue to bring him off the bench.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Collin Sexton (LAL): Collin Sexton (head) finished Wednesday’s win over the Bucks with 10 points (4-of-8 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), one rebound, three assists and one steal.
item.description:
Collin Sexton (head) finished Wednesday’s win over the Bucks with 10 points (4-of-8 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), one rebound, three assists and one steal.

With Quentin Grimes (finger) unavailable for Wednesday’s game, Sexton’s role had added importance. Unfortunately, while he did hit double figures, the Lakers guard had to leave with just under seven minutes left in the fourth quarter. Sexton banged heads with Bucks guard Ryan Rollins, and both left the game and did not return. Sexton’s cut required sutures, but there were no reports that he might have to enter the league’s concussion protocol.

Raphielle Johnson

Fonte: Dan Woike

item.title: [Recap] Walker Kessler (LAL): Walker Kessler amassed 10 points (5-of-10 FGs), 11 rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block in Wednesday’s win over the Bucks.
item.description:
Walker Kessler amassed 10 points (5-of-10 FGs), 11 rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block in Wednesday’s win over the Bucks.

The Lakers have played seven games in November, and Kessler has recorded a double-double in six of them. In addition to the double-doubles, the 7-footer has blocked at least one shot in 11 of 13 games this season. Thus far, Kessler has been everything that fantasy managers hoped he would be in Los Angeles, and then some.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Sandro Mamukelashvili (LAL): Sandro Mamukelashvili accounted for 23 points (9-of-15 FGs), three rebounds, two assists, one steal and five three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Bucks.
item.description:
Sandro Mamukelashvili accounted for 23 points (9-of-15 FGs), three rebounds, two assists, one steal and five three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Bucks.

Mamukelashvili was at his best during the second quarter, shooting 4-of-4 from the field and scoring 10 points. He didn’t provide much beyond points and three-pointers, but Mamu has been productive enough this season to merit a roster spot in deep leagues. Despite not playing the same position, Mamukelashvili would be worth streaming if either Luka Dončić (ankle) or Austin Reaves (heel) misses Friday’s game against the Spurs.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Injury] Trey Murphy (NOP): Trey Murphy (knee) is out for Wednesday’s game against the Nets.
item.description:
Trey Murphy (knee) is out for Wednesday’s game against the Nets.

Downgraded from probable to doubtful late Wednesday morning, Murphy will miss a second straight game. Saddiq Bey started Monday’s loss to the Warriors but offered little production. However, Wednesday’s matchup should be a better one for him.

Raphielle Johnson

While he can be inconsistent, McCain is on a bit of a heater, scoring 21, 19 and 21 points in his last three games.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Shai Gilgeous-Alexander (OKC): Shai Gilgeous-Alexander recorded 26 points (8-of-22 FGs, 10-of-11 FTs), eight rebounds, three assists and one block in Tuesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.
item.description:
Shai Gilgeous-Alexander recorded 26 points (8-of-22 FGs, 10-of-11 FTs), eight rebounds, three assists and one block in Tuesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers.

After playing the entire third quarter, Gilgeous-Alexander did not play at all in the fourth, as Portland managed to pull away. Due to Oklahoma City’s many injuries, the two-time MVP is being asked to do even more heavy lifting on offense. SGA’s field-goal percentage suffered on Tuesday, but that doesn’t do much to change his status as one of the most valuable players to roster in fantasy basketball. Oklahoma City plays Portland again on Wednesday, and the extra rest time he picked up in the fourth quarter on Tuesday could pay dividends for SGA.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Sidy Cissoko (POR): Sidy Cissoko recorded 17 points (5-of-14 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), three rebounds, three assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Thunder.
item.description:

Trail Blazers head coach Micah Nori made a change to his starting lineup on Tuesday, replacing Scoot Henderson with Cissoko. While he didn’t shoot well from the field, Sidy finished with a season-high point total and a solid overall stat line in 33 minutes. Henderson played 23 minutes and finished with 11 points, one rebound, four assists and three three-pointers. Cissoko isn’t a must-add, but he’s worth watching, especially with Ja Morant (hamstring) out for a few more weeks.

Raphielle Johnson

item.description:

Avdija and Damian Lillard took over the third quarter of Tuesday’s 123-103 victory, combining to score 22 of the Trail Blazers’ 38 points. The former supplemented his nine points with three rebounds and three assists in the period, and Deni has scored at least 21 points in eight of Portland’s 10 games. The two teams meet again on Wednesday in what could be another big night for Avdija, who finished Tuesday’s win two assists shy of a double-double.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Damian Lillard (POR): Damian Lillard amassed 25 points (8-of-15 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), three rebounds, three assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Thunder.
item.description:
Damian Lillard amassed 25 points (8-of-15 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), three rebounds, three assists, one steal and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Thunder.

Fans got to see “vintage Dame” during the third quarter, with his production helping Portland grab control of the season. Shooting 5-of-6 from the field, Lillard scored 13 points in the third. Lillard didn’t play in the fourth quarter, and the 24 minutes he did play may ensure he’s available for Wednesday’s rematch.

item.title: [Recap] Luka Dončić (LAL): Luka Dončić accumulated 32 points (11-of-22 FGs, 7-of-7 FTs), eight rebounds, 10 assists, five steals and two blocks over 39 minutes to lead the Lakers to a 124-114 win over the Hawks on Monday.
item.description:
Luka Dončić accumulated 32 points (11-of-22 FGs, 7-of-7 FTs), eight rebounds, 10 assists, five steals and two blocks over 39 minutes to lead the Lakers to a 124-114 win over the Hawks on Monday.

Dončić fell short of the 40-point plateau in his return from a one-game absence due to a minor back issue, but showed no signs of rust, turning in another spectacular all-around performance that left him two rebounds shy of a triple-double. He scored 18 of his 32 points after halftime, helping Los Angeles withstand a late Atlanta rally before pulling away in the closing minutes. The Lakers were also without Austin Reaves (illness) in this one, making Dončić’s latest all-around performance even more impressive. The 27-year-old franchise cornerstone has been virtually unstoppable through the early stages of the season and has quickly established himself as the frontrunner in the MVP race.
